_note: aniq_baseline_independent_cnn_v2: first improved CNN, built on aniq_baseline_independent_cnn (two separate networks, crop and disease, same data, augmentation, loss, optimiser and validation protocol). Three changes: (1) ConvNeXt-Tiny instead of ResNet-50 (stronger ImageNet backbone, same 224 px input); (2) max_epochs 30 instead of 20, because the baseline selected epoch 18 of 20, so its validation curve was still rising at the cap; (3) a 'composition' section: the pair score becomes 2 * (w * log P(crop) + (1 - w) * log P(disease)) with each head logit-adjusted by tau (see the section's _note), w and tau chosen on validation together with the epoch and gamma. The in-run 'plain_scoring' entry in metrics.json (val) scores the same networks the baseline way (w 0.5, tau 0), which isolates change (3); changes (1) and (2) are not separated.

data._note: Same splits and 333-pair protocol as the CLIP versions (generalised zero-shot).

model._note: ConvNeXt-Tiny (torchvision IMAGENET1K_V1, about 28M parameters, similar to ResNet-50's 25M) instead of ResNet-50. One linear head per target with dropout 0.3, as in the baseline.

input._note: Images are pre-resized once to shorter side 256 (runs/cache/resized_256) so training is not bottlenecked on decoding 3120 px JPEGs. Train: random resized crop 224. Test: resize 256, centre crop 224. ImageNet mean/std.

augmentation._note: Standard field-robustness augmentation: random resized crop (scale 0.25-1), horizontal and vertical flips (leaf orientation is arbitrary), brightness/contrast/saturation jitter 0.2. No hue jitter: colour is diagnostic (yellow halos, orange rust, purple tints), see the symptom research.

loss._note: Cross-entropy with label smoothing 0.1 (long-tailed, noisy labels: median 7 images per pair). For the multi-task model the two head losses are summed with equal weight.

composition._note: How the two heads are combined into the 333 pair scores, chosen on validation (grids are [start, stop, step], stop exclusive, as gamma_grid). crop_weight w: score = 2 * (w * log P(crop) + (1 - w) * log P(disease)); the two networks are trained separately, so their confidences are not on a common scale, and crop is the more reliable head (baseline test-seen: crop 80%, disease 62.5%). The factor 2 keeps the baseline scale, so w 0.5 is exactly the baseline and gamma_grid keeps its meaning. tau: post-hoc logit adjustment (Menon et al., 2021), each head's log-probs minus tau * log(training class frequency), renormalised; targets the long tail (baseline seen top-1 54.9% per image but 35.8% per-class mean). tau 0 = off, 1 = full correction to a uniform prior. Priors come from the images each network was trained on (the fit split in stage 1, all train in stage 2).

optimizer._note: AdamW; backbone 1e-4 (pretrained, small steps), heads 1e-3 (random init), weight decay 0.05. Cosine decay per step over the run.

validation._note: Same validation split procedure and settings as v6 (pseudo-unseen pairs held out, healthy excluded, 40 images per held-out pair, real unseen pairs hidden), so gamma is chosen the same way for baselines and the proposed model. gamma_grid is in log-probability units here (pair score = sum of two log-probs), so its range differs from the CLIP versions' cosine units: 0 to 10, step 0.1.

training._note: Batch 32, AMP (channels-last was 4.5x slower on this GPU, see train_cnn.py). max_epochs bounds stage 1; stage 2 refits on all training images for the selected epoch count.

evaluation._note: Pair score = log P(crop) + log P(disease). gamma (subtracted from seen pairs) from validation, in log-probability units.

runtime._note: 2 dataloader workers (was 4): the first run crashed with Windows error 1455 (out of virtual memory) in its final refit after finishing validation (val HM 58.86%); each worker commits ~1.4 GB. Images come from the resized cache.
